easy.def: To move from one place to another.
examples: I go to school by bus.
We went to the park.
The train goes fast.

more.def: To move or travel from one place to another, or to leave a place.
examples: Every summer we go to the lake for a week.
The ducks went down the stream in a line.
She has gone to the library to return her books.

easy.def: Something you want to do and work hard for.
examples: My goal is to read ten books.
I kicked the ball to score a goal.
His goal is to learn to swim.

more.def: Something you are trying to reach or achieve.
examples: Her goal is to learn to play the violin this year.
Our class goal is to collect five hundred cans of food.
He set a goal to save enough money for a bike.

easy.def: The player who guards the goal.
examples: The goalie saved the ball.
Our goalie is tall.
The goalie dived.

more.def: The player in a game such as soccer or hockey whose job is to stop the ball or puck from going into the goal.
examples: The goalie dived and stopped the ball with her fingertips.
Our goalie wears special gloves and a helmet.
The goalie kicked the ball far downfield.

easy.def: The player who guards the goal.
examples: The goalkeeper caught the ball.
She is our goalkeeper.
The goalkeeper jumped high.

more.def: The player on a team whose job is to stop the ball from going into the goal.
examples: The goalkeeper dived and caught the ball just before it crossed the line.
Our goalkeeper wears gloves to help her grip the ball.
The goalkeeper kicked the ball far down the field.

easy.def: A farm animal with horns that likes to climb.
examples: The goat ate grass.
The goat has a beard.
A goat climbed the hill.

more.def: A farm animal with horns and a short tail that is raised for milk, meat or wool.
examples: The goat climbed to the top of the rock.
We got milk from the goat.
A baby goat is called a kid.

easy.def: To eat very fast.
examples: The dog gobbled its food.
He gobbled his lunch.
Don't gobble your food.

more.def: To eat food very quickly, often in big bites.
examples: The hungry puppy gobbled up its dinner in just a few seconds.
He gobbled down his sandwich so he could go out to play.
The ducks gobbled the bread crumbs we threw.

easy.def: To make the sound a turkey makes.
examples: The turkey gobbled loudly.
Turkeys gobble in the farm.
I heard it gobble.

more.def: To make the loud, bubbling call that a male turkey makes.
examples: The turkey gobbled loudly as we walked past the pen.
In the spring, wild turkeys gobble to call each other.
We heard a turkey gobble in the woods early in the morning.

easy.def: A big cup with a stem.
examples: The king held a goblet.
A goblet of water.
The goblet is silver.

more.def: A drinking cup with a stem and a foot, often made of glass or metal.
examples: The king raised a golden goblet at the feast.
She set a glass goblet of water at each place at the table.
The goblet was decorated with tiny jewels.

easy.def: A small, ugly creature in fairy tales.
examples: A goblin hid under the bridge.
The goblin laughed.
We read about a goblin.

more.def: A small, wicked or tricky creature in fairy tales that is often ugly and likes to play tricks.
examples: In the fairy tale, a goblin lived under the bridge and played tricks on travelers.
The goblin hid the farmer's tools in the barn.
The story is about a brave girl who outsmarted a goblin.

easy.def: A girl who has a godparent.
examples: She is my goddaughter.
My goddaughter is six.
I gave a gift to my goddaughter.

more.def: A girl or woman for whom someone is a godparent.
examples: The woman held her goddaughter at the ceremony.
She sent a card to her goddaughter.
My goddaughter visited for the summer.

easy.def: A female god in stories and religions.
examples: The goddess lived on a mountain.
A goddess is a female god.
The goddess had magic powers.

more.def: A female god, as in the myths of ancient Greece and Rome.
examples: In the myth, the goddess lived on a mountain.
The Greeks prayed to a goddess of the harvest.
The goddess of the sea calmed the waves.

easy.def: A woman who promises to help look after a child.
examples: My godmother sent a gift.
The fairy godmother helped.
She is my godmother.

more.def: A woman who promises at a child's naming ceremony to help take care of that child; also a kind magical helper in fairy tales.
examples: My godmother sent me a book for my birthday.
In the story, the fairy godmother turned a pumpkin into a coach.
She is the godmother of my little cousin.

easy.def: A boy who has a godparent.
examples: He is my godson.
My godson came to visit.
The godson is six.

more.def: A boy or man for whom someone is a godparent.
examples: My uncle gave a gift to his godson.
She sent a card to her godson.
The godson visited every summer.

easy.def: To stare with wide eyes.
examples: Do not goggle.
The kids goggled at the cake.
He goggled at the show.

more.def: To stare with wide-open eyes in surprise.
examples: The kids goggled at the huge cake.
He goggled at the strange machine.
She goggled in amazement.

easy.def: Special glasses that cover your eyes to keep them safe.
examples: I wear goggles to swim.
The goggles keep out water.
Put on your goggles.

more.def: Special glasses that fit tightly around the eyes to protect them from water, wind, dust or chemicals.
examples: I wear goggles when I swim so that the water does not sting my eyes.
The scientist put on safety goggles before the experiment.
He pulled his ski goggles down over his eyes.

easy.def: A shiny yellow metal.
examples: The ring is gold.
Pirates look for gold.
The crown is made of gold.

more.def: A shiny yellow metal that is valuable and used to make jewelry.
examples: The crown was made of solid gold.
Miners once searched the river for gold.
She wears a gold ring.

easy.def: Shiny and yellow, like the metal.
examples: A gold star.
Gold stickers.
Her dress was gold.

more.def: Having the shiny yellow color of the precious metal.
examples: She won a gold medal.
The gold sunset lit the lake.
He glued gold stars to the card.

easy.def: Shiny yellow, like gold.
examples: The golden sun shone.
She has golden hair.
The prize was a golden cup.

more.def: Shiny yellow like gold, or made of gold.
examples: The golden wheat swayed in the breeze.
The queen wore a golden crown.
The leaves turned golden in the fall.

easy.def: A small orange fish kept as a pet.
examples: I have a goldfish.
The goldfish swims in a bowl.
We fed the goldfish.

more.def: A small orange or gold fish that people often keep as a pet in a bowl or pond.
examples: I feed my goldfish a few flakes of food each morning.
Goldfish swam under the lily pads in the garden pond.
Our class won a goldfish at the school fair.

easy.def: A game where you hit a small ball into holes with a club.
examples: Grandpa plays golf.
Golf is played outside.
We played mini golf.

more.def: A game in which players use clubs to hit a small ball into a series of holes.
examples: Grandpa plays golf on Saturday mornings.
The golf course has wide green grass.
In golf, the player with the fewest hits wins.

easy.def: A person who plays golf.
examples: The golfer hit the ball.
A golfer swung.
My dad is a golfer.

more.def: A person who plays golf, a sport in which you hit a small ball into holes using clubs.
examples: The golfer hit the ball across the green.
My grandpa is a golfer and plays every Saturday.
The golfer cheered when her ball dropped into the hole.

easy.def: A word that shows surprise.
examples: Golly, that is big!
Golly, look at that!
Oh golly!

more.def: An old-fashioned word that people say when they are surprised.
examples: Golly, that is a big fish!
Oh golly, I forgot my hat!
Golly, what a nice surprise!

easy.def: A long, narrow boat used in Venice.
examples: We rode a gondola.
The gondola glides.
A gondola has a long oar.

more.def: A long, narrow boat with high ends, used on the canals of Venice, or a car that hangs from a cable.
examples: We rode a gondola down the canal in Venice.
The gondola carried skiers up the mountain.
A man rowed the gondola.

easy.def: A thick, sticky, wet stuff.
examples: I stepped in goo.
The goo is green.
Goo dripped on the floor.

more.def: A thick, sticky, wet substance.
examples: The slime was a green goo that stuck to our fingers.
I stepped in a puddle of mud and goo.
Honey is a golden goo that stretches off the spoon.

easy.def: Nice, and just right.
examples: This is a good book.
She is a good friend.
The soup smells good.

more.def: Of a high quality, pleasant, or helpful.
examples: Sunshine and rain are good for the garden.
He is a good swimmer and has won many races.
It is a good idea to wear a helmet.

easy.def: Kind and doing what is right.
examples: He is a good boy.
She was good to the new girl.
Be good for the sitter.

more.def: Behaving well, and showing kindness or honesty.
examples: The good neighbor shoveled snow from our walk.
Our puppy was very good at the vet's office.
It was a good thing to return the lost wallet.

easy.def: A word you say when you leave.
examples: Goodbye, Grandma!
We said goodbye at the door.
Wave goodbye.

more.def: Something you say when you or another person is leaving.
examples: She waved and called goodbye from the bus window.
We said goodbye to our friends at the end of camp.
Goodbye, everyone; see you tomorrow!

easy.def: A treat that is nice to eat.
examples: We had goodies at the party.
Grandma baked some goodies.
I got a bag of goodies.

more.def: A treat or a nice thing to eat or have, such as a sweet or a gift.
examples: Grandma baked goodies for the party, including cookies and cupcakes.
Each child took home a bag of goodies.
The picnic basket was full of goodies.

easy.def: Being good.
examples: I believe in goodness.
Her goodness shines.
The goodness of a kind heart.

more.def: The quality of being good or kind.
examples: We admired her goodness.
The goodness of the people made the town warm.
His goodness showed when he helped the lost child.

easy.def: A word you say to show surprise.
examples: My goodness!
Goodness me!
Thank goodness!

more.def: A word used to show surprise or relief.
examples: My goodness, what a big dog!
Thank goodness you are safe!
Goodness, it is late.

easy.def: A word you say at bedtime.
examples: Goodnight, Mom.
I said goodnight.
Goodnight, sleep tight.

more.def: A word you say to someone before going to sleep.
examples: Goodnight, Mom, I love you.
I said goodnight and turned off the light.
"Goodnight, sleep tight," said Dad.

easy.def: Things that are made to be sold.
examples: The store sells goods.
The truck carries goods.
The ship brought goods.

more.def: Things that people make, buy and sell.
examples: The shop sells goods from around the world.
Trucks carry goods from the factory to stores.
The ship delivered goods to the port.

easy.def: Kind feelings and a wish to help.
examples: She showed goodwill.
A smile shows goodwill.
Goodwill makes friends.

more.def: A friendly, kind feeling toward others.
examples: She showed goodwill to the new student.
The gift was a sign of goodwill.
Goodwill makes it easier to make friends.

easy.def: A treat to eat.
examples: Mom brought goodies.
I ate a goody.
The bag was full of goodies.

more.def: A tasty treat, or something nice.
examples: Mom brought goodies to the party.
The bag was full of cookies and other goodies.
We shared the goodies after the game.

easy.def: Soft and sticky.
examples: The cake is gooey.
I like gooey cheese.
The gooey mud stuck.

more.def: Soft, wet and sticky.
examples: The gooey cheese stretched on the pizza.
I made a gooey mess with the honey.
The gooey mud stuck to my boots.

easy.def: To make a silly mistake.
examples: I goofed on my spelling.
She goofed up the game.
He goofed and dropped it.

more.def: To make a silly mistake, or to play around and act silly.
examples: I goofed on the last spelling word.
We goofed around at recess and laughed a lot.
He goofed and put salt in the cake instead of sugar.

easy.def: A silly mistake.
examples: That was a goof.
I made a goof.
The goof was funny.

more.def: A silly mistake, or a person who acts silly.
examples: That was a silly goof on my part.
My brother is such a goof that he makes everyone laugh.
She made a goof and put on two different socks.

easy.def: A silly person.
examples: My brother is a goofball.
The goofball made a face.
He is a goofball.

more.def: A silly, joking person who likes to make people laugh.
examples: My little brother is such a goofball.
The goofball wore a funny hat to school.
She is a goofball who makes us all laugh.

easy.def: Silly.
examples: The clown is goofy.
I made a goofy face.
The goofy dog tripped.

more.def: Silly and playful in a funny way.
examples: I made a goofy face in the mirror.
The goofy puppy chased its tail.
He wore a goofy hat to the party.

easy.def: A big bird with a long neck that swims.
examples: The goose honked.
A goose swam in the pond.
Geese fly south.

more.def: A large water bird with a long neck and webbed feet.
examples: The goose honked and flapped its wings.
A flock of geese flew south in a V.
The goose swam across the pond.

easy.def: A small animal that digs tunnels under the ground.
examples: A gopher dug a hole.
The gopher lives underground.
I saw a gopher.

more.def: A small furry animal with big front teeth and strong claws that digs tunnels and lives underground.
examples: A gopher dug a tunnel under the garden and ate the carrots.
The gopher popped its head out of a hole.
Gophers use their big front teeth and strong claws to dig.

easy.def: A deep, narrow valley with steep sides.
examples: A river runs through the gorge.
The gorge is deep.
We hiked the gorge.

more.def: A deep, narrow valley with steep rocky sides, usually with a river running through it.
examples: A river rushed through the deep gorge below us.
We hiked along the rim of the gorge.
The bridge crosses the gorge.

easy.def: To eat far too much.
examples: Do not gorge on candy.
He gorged on cake.
The bear gorged on fish.

more.def: To eat a very large amount, more than you need.
examples: The bear gorged on salmon before winter.
Do not gorge on candy, or you will feel sick.
He gorged himself on pizza at the party.

easy.def: Very, very pretty.
examples: The sunset was gorgeous.
She has a gorgeous smile.
The garden looks gorgeous.

more.def: Very beautiful, so lovely that you stop and look.
examples: The sky was a gorgeous pink at sunset.
She wore a gorgeous gown to the ball.
The mountains looked gorgeous after the first snow.

easy.def: A very big, strong ape.
examples: The gorilla sat in the zoo.
A gorilla is big.
The gorilla ate a banana.

more.def: The largest kind of ape, with a strong body and black fur, that lives in Africa.
examples: The gorilla beat its chest in the zoo.
A gorilla can weigh over three hundred pounds.
The baby gorilla clung to its mother.

easy.def: A word you say when you are surprised.
examples: Gosh, it's big!
Gosh, what a day!
Oh gosh!

more.def: A word used to show surprise.
examples: "Gosh, that is a huge cake!" said Mia.
Gosh, I forgot my homework.
"Oh gosh," he said, "it's already noon."

easy.def: A kind of religious music.
examples: The choir sang gospel.
I like gospel music.
We heard a gospel song.

more.def: A style of religious music with strong singing and a lively beat.
examples: The choir sang gospel in church.
I like gospel music because it is joyful.
We heard a gospel song at the festival.

easy.def: Talk about other people that may not be true.
examples: Do not spread gossip.
The gossip hurt her.
I do not like gossip.

more.def: Talk about other people's private lives, which is often unkind or untrue.
examples: Do not listen to gossip about your friends.
The gossip about the new girl was not true.
Gossip can hurt people's feelings.

easy.def: A thick stew with meat and paprika.
examples: We ate goulash.
The goulash is hot.
Goulash is a stew.

more.def: A thick stew of meat and vegetables flavored with paprika.
examples: We ate goulash for dinner.
The goulash was hot and spicy.
Grandma cooked goulash in a big pot.

easy.def: A hard-shelled fruit like a squash.
examples: We grew a gourd.
The gourd is hard.
A gourd looks like a pumpkin.

more.def: A fruit with a hard shell that grows on a vine and is used as a bowl or decoration.
examples: We carved a gourd for the fall display.
The gourd dried into a hard shell.
Colorful gourds sat on the table in autumn.

easy.def: Very fine and fancy, as food.
examples: We ate a gourmet meal.
The gourmet cheese was good.
A gourmet chef.

more.def: Describing food that is of very high quality and prepared with great care.
examples: The chef served a gourmet meal with five courses.
The shop sold gourmet cheese from around the world.
They ate a gourmet dinner at the fancy restaurant.

easy.def: To lead and make the rules for a country or town.
examples: The mayor governs the town.
Rules govern the game.
The king governed the land.

more.def: To lead a country, a state or a town by making and carrying out the laws and rules.
examples: The mayor and the council govern our town.
The king governed the land wisely for many years.
Rules govern how the game is played.

easy.def: A woman who taught children at their home, long ago.
examples: The governess taught the girls.
A governess lived with them.
The governess read to the child.

more.def: A woman who was paid to live in a family's home and teach their children, especially in the past.
examples: The governess taught the children reading and math at home.
In the old story, the governess lived with the family in the big house.
The governess took the children for a walk each afternoon.

easy.def: The people who lead a country or state.
examples: The government makes laws.
The mayor works for the government.
There is a new government.

more.def: The group of people who rule a country, state or town and make its laws.
examples: The government built a new highway.
Our town's government plans the parks.
Leaders in the government met to talk.

easy.def: Having to do with the government.
examples: A governmental office.
The governmental rule.
A governmental building.

more.def: Having to do with a government, which is the group that runs a country or town.
examples: The city hall is a governmental building.
A governmental office issues driver licenses.
She works in a governmental agency.

easy.def: The leader of a state.
examples: Our governor visited the school.
The governor gave a speech.
She wants to be governor.

more.def: A person who is elected to lead the government of a state.
examples: The governor signed a new law for our state.
Each state in the country has its own governor.
The governor spoke at the opening of the new park.

easy.def: A long, fancy dress.
examples: She wore a gown.
The gown is blue.
The princess wore a gown.

more.def: A long, formal dress, or a loose robe worn for a special event.
examples: She wore a long gown to the ball.
The graduates wore caps and gowns.
The queen's gown sparkled.
